resources.string: Turns the Beauty-R1 remote’s swipe buttons into next, previous, volume and play/pause.

Shizuku: %1$s
Grab service: %2$s
Accessibility fallback: %3$s

While the grab service is running the remote’s d-pad works without showing a cursor. Otherwise, the accessibility fallback handles it, but the cursor still appears.

R1 BT Remote uses Android’s AccessibilityService API as a fallback for when Shizuku isn’t running.

Why it’s needed: the Beauty-R1 remote pretends to be a touchscreen, so each button press arrives as a fake swipe or tap. The accessibility service intercepts this pointer input, and the remote’s held left/right presses, and turns them into media controls: play/pause, next and previous track, fast forward, rewind and volume.

While it’s on, mouse-pointer input goes to the service rather than to other apps. The service doesn’t read screen content or what you type, and the app doesn’t collect, store or share any data.

Tap Agree to open Android’s accessibility settings, where you can turn on R1 BT Remote. You can turn it off there at any time.
